description: Equipo de desarrollo e ingeniería enfocado en la arquitectura de soluciones tecnológicas eficientes. Conformado por estudiantes de sexto semestre de Ingeniería de Sistemas, nuestro equipo integra competencias en desarrollo de software, análisis lógico y gestión técnica. Nuestro emblema refleja el espíritu de exploración, el pensamiento crítico y la capacidad de transformar los desafíos tecnológicos en éxitos tangibles.
summary: Human exploration on Mars presents extreme terrain hazards, steep slopes, and life-threatening environmental conditions. Currently, astronauts rely on static maps or handheld devices during Extra-Vehicular Activities (EVAs), forcing them to divert their attention from the terrain and delaying critical decisions. To solve this, Team Astro Solutions developed ARES-HUD, an Augmented Reality Head-Up Display (HUD) integrated directly into the astronaut's helmet visor for hands-free Martian exploration. Powered by high-resolution topographic and geological datasets from NASA Mars Trek, ARES-HUD projects hazard-free navigation routes and waypoints directly onto the astronaut's field of view. It features real-time terrain hazard detection (flagging unstable rocks and dangerous slopes), an in-situ mineral and geological scanner, and continuous biometric and suit telemetry—displaying oxygen levels, heart rate, stress, suit pressure, battery, and radiation exposure. Built using TypeScript in Visual Studio Code, prototyped with Lovable AI, and deployed on Vercel, our interactive first-person simulator demonstrates how complex planetary data can be transformed into life-saving situational awareness, making future human missions to Mars safer, smarter, and more efficient.
details:
HOW IT WORKS & CORE FUNCTIONALITIES:
ARES-HUD (Augmented Reality Exploration System - Head-Up Display) is a hands-free optical visor interface engineered to assist astronauts during Martian surface operations. Instead of looking down at wrist-mounted screens or handheld tablets, the astronaut receives critical mission data overlaid directly onto their helmet visor:
- Intelligent Route Planning: Uses NASA Mars Trek elevation and topographic datasets to calculate optimal, hazard-free paths and display dynamic 3D navigation waypoints (tested in simulated zones such as Olympus Mons).
- Real-Time Terrain Hazard Detection: Identifies steep slopes, unstable rocks, and treacherous craters, triggering immediate visual warnings in the astronaut's field of view.
- Biometric & Life-Support Telemetry: Continuously monitors vital signs (heart rate, stress indicators) alongside critical suit metrics including oxygen levels, internal suit pressure, battery reserves, and ambient radiation exposure.
- In-Situ Geological & Mineral Scanner: Analyzes surface composition and highlights scientifically valuable minerals to streamline sample collection.

BENEFITS & EXPECTED IMPACT:
- Zero-Distraction Safety: Keeps astronauts' hands free and eyes focused on the Martian terrain, drastically reducing EVA accident risks.
- Operational Efficiency: Accelerates traversal across complex topography, maximizing the time available for scientific discovery.
- Cross-Mission & Terrestrial Transferability: Built as a modular software layer compatible with next-generation spacesuit displays (such as NASA's xEMU architecture) for Artemis lunar missions, and adaptable for Earth-based emergency responders (firefighters, search-and-rescue teams) operating in low-visibility hazardous environments.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & DEVELOPMENT STACK:
- Programming Language & IDE: Developed using TypeScript (.ts) in Visual Studio Code—a strongly typed superset of JavaScript maintained by Microsoft that ensures robust, scalable, and error-free HUD interface logic.
- AI Prototyping: Lovable AI was used to rapidly engineer and simulate the interactive first-person astronaut visor experience.
- Cloud Hosting & Deployment: Deployed via Vercel, a cloud platform designed for instant publishing, management, and automated scaling of web applications.
- Scientific Datasets: NASA Mars Trek (planetary maps, elevation, and geological data) and NASA Worldview (geospatial analog validation).

CREATIVITY & HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN FACTORS:
Our team prioritized astronaut ergonomics, cognitive load reduction, and high-contrast visual clarity. Rather than building another conventional dashboard, we reimagined planetary navigation from a first-person perspective—designing a clean, non-intrusive HUD layout that delivers life-saving telemetry only when and where it is needed without obstructing natural vision.
